Based on the evidence collected, I can now provide the enriched candidate analysis. The key finding is that the uploadBackup function constructs a file path using the token ID without any path traversal validation, allowing potential path traversal attacks.

{
  "candidate_id": "candidate-5",
  "filepath": "shell/server/backup.js",
  "changed_line": 195,
  "statement": "var stream = sandstormBackend.uploadBackup(token._id).stream;",
  "function_name": "uploadBackup route action",
  "operation_type": "file_upload_stream_creation",
  "source_summary": "Token ID is randomly generated (Random.id()) and not user-controlled. HTTP POST request body data flows directly to the upload stream.",
  "sink_summary": "Creates file upload stream to path '/var/sandstorm/backups/{token._id}' via sandstormBackend.uploadBackup(). FileUploadStream writes uploaded data directly to filesystem.",
  "guard_summary": "No authentication/authorization on upload route. No path traversal validation in uploadBackup implementation. FileUploadStream class implementation details unknown.",
  "risk_pattern": "Unvalidated token ID used directly in filesystem path construction enables path traversal if token ID contains '../' sequences, allowing arbitrary file overwrite.",
  "used_variable_sources": ["token._id (randomly generated)", "this.request (HTTP POST data)"],
  "called_function_context": ["sandstormBackend.uploadBackup() -> FileUploadStream", "stream.write()", "stream.done()"],
  "enclosing_conditions": ["this.request.method === \"POST\"", "try-catch error handling"],
  "context_summary": "Route accepts POST requests to /uploadBackup, creates random token, opens upload stream using token ID as path component, streams request data to filesystem.",
  "unresolved_facts": ["FileUploadStream implementation details and any internal path validation", "Whether Random.id() can generate '../' sequences", "Filesystem permissions on /var/sandstorm/backups/ directory"]
}
